text:
harpreet: Quickstart blocker - new hire on company laptop ran `brew install redwoodctl` then `redwoodctl init` and `redwoodctl login --headless`. Browser redirected but CLI never got the callback.

eva: what does the CLI show?

harpreet: `waiting for callback at http://127.0.0.1:12345` forever, then a flood of `login failed: tls: handshake error` after a minute.

noah: two likely causes: corp TLS inspection (x509 unknown authority) or bind/namespace issue (WSL, Docker, VM).

harpreet: They were on WSL2 with Docker desktop. Also their env includes `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/corp.pem`. `curl` works with `--cacert`, but redwoodctl ignores that and fails.

eva: redwoodctl currently uses system root CAs and doesn't read SSL_CERT_FILE. That's a DX leak. We should detect that env var in `redwoodctl doctor` and warn.

noah: Agreed. Short-term fixes: 1) doctor detects SSL_CERT_FILE / REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and prints a clear hint, 2) add a `--trust-local-ca /path/to/ca.pem` flag scoped to headless login (session-only), 3) expose `--local-callback-host` in help and improve postinstall messaging to mention `--profile quickstart` and device-code fallback.

harpreet: `--trust-local-ca` would have helped here — explicit dev-only CA for the headless flow. Make it non-persistent and warn loudly.

eva: Also the CLI retries are too aggressive and produce confusing logs. Let's change default backoff to exponential and show one actionable hint after 10s instead of spamming the log.

noah: For container/WSL detection we can check /proc/1/cgroup or common env vars and suggest `--local-callback-host=0.0.0.0` or `--device-code`. Don't auto-bind 0.0.0.0 by default.

harpreet: Another onboarding issue: `redwoodctl init` quietly re-used an existing `default` profile and the quickstart app expects `quickstart`. New hire assumed init created quickstart and got confused.

eva: Make `init` interactive by default when a profile collision occurs and print a one-line summary of created files and the active profile. Also update the Homebrew postinstall text to `redwoodctl init --profile quickstart` so sample apps wire correctly.

ci-bot: deploy-check: docs branch `devex/cli-trust-local-ca-doctor` lint OK

noah: Good. For error messages, map `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` to a hint: "If you're on a corporate network with TLS inspection, add your CA to system trust or use `redwoodctl login --trust-local-ca /path/to/ca.pem` (dev-only)." Include link to docs.

harpreet: I'll file a ticket with steps, include the WSL/Docker notes and the stack traces. Will propose a tiny PR for doctor + postinstall text + retry backoff.

eva: Thanks. Also add unit/integration test to the CLI that simulates SSL_CERT_FILE behavior so we don't regress.

noah: Tagging devex and eng-platform. Thanks! :thumbsup:
